headline: Highest risk is data leakage from Chatwoot’s broad egress into a local-only, no-filesystem marker workflow; prompt-injection and capability-conflict risks are otherwise limited by marker’s disabled I/O.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can ingest and emit customer messages and integrates with Slack/Dialogflow/Shopify/Linear, while marker has no browser, MCP, filesystem, or network surfaces. A direct injection bridge is not documented, so the pair only plausibly connects through manual handoff or exported text, making hijack risk limited.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is manually copied into marker as document text, prompt-like content can be reinterpreted.
IF an operator routes Chatwoot transcripts into marker without sanitization, embedded instructions may survive.
mitigations: Strip instructions from copied transcripts before processing.
Use a fixed template for any Chatwoot-to-marker handoff.
Review marker inputs for prompt-like directives before ingestion.
Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to all transferred text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, and has broad network egress. Marker is local-only with no network egress and no filesystem read/write, so the main leakage path is Chatwoot data being exported or copied into marker for processing; that exists in default workflows but is not automatic.
conditions: IF Chatwoot transcripts or customer records are exported into marker, sensitive customer data can be exposed in the processing workflow.
IF marker outputs are stored back into Chatwoot without redaction, customer data may be duplicated across systems.
mitigations: Redact customer identifiers before export.
Process only synthetic or minimized samples.
Keep marker offline from any shared storage.
Delete temporary exports immediately after use.
requires-engineering: enforce field-level data-loss prevention on Chatwoot exports.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress, but marker explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shell, or spawn subprocesses. With no overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource documented, there is no plausible capability conflict between the pair.
conditions: IF marker is deployed with additional write or shell permissions not shown in the profile, conflict risk would need reassessment.
mitigations: Keep marker in its documented read-only mode.
Avoid sharing mutable directories between the tools.
Do not grant marker git or shell permissions.
Monitor for unexpected permission changes.
requires-engineering: add orchestration locks if write access is later enabled.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can produce customer-facing content and marker can transform documents, but marker has no action-taking authority and no documented automation path back into Chatwoot. Without a verified pipeline where marker treats Chatwoot output as authoritative, cascading error is limited to manual misuse.
conditions: IF an operator pastes Chatwoot-generated text into marker and then republishes it without review, errors can propagate.
IF marker output is used as a source for customer replies, hallucinated or malformed content may be forwarded.
mitigations: Require human review before publishing any derived text.
Use marker only for formatting, not factual generation.
Label Chatwoot-originated content as unverified.
Compare outputs against source records before sending.
requires-engineering: add approval gates before customer-facing use.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot clearly handles customer data and messages, while marker’s profile shows no touched data classes or residency/compliance constraints. The only documented compliance concern is that customer data could be moved from Chatwoot into marker during manual processing, but the pair does not show a built-in residency or certification mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is exported from Chatwoot into marker, retention and access controls must be rechecked.
IF marker outputs are retained alongside Chatwoot records, deletion/export workflows may diverge.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated records to marker.
Minimize retained copies of processed documents.
Document a deletion workflow for temporary exports.
Confirm retention settings before each batch.
requires-engineering: align retention and audit logging across both systems.
